title: Cache deliberate file versions
summary: Caching lets browsers reuse files. Long caching works best for files whose names change when their contents change.
introduction: Caching lets browsers reuse files. Long caching works best for files whose names change when their contents change. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Caching lets browsers reuse files. Long caching works best for files whose names change when their contents change.
This fragment permits a one-hour freshness period for matching responses. The correct policy depends on how the files are versioned.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Compare caching app.abc123.js with an unversioned index.html.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not cache a frequently updated HTML page for a year without a plan to refresh it.
For more detail later, use this [Nginx further reading](https://nginx.org/en/docs/beginners_guide.html).
